title.en: Constrained gear motion from one driver

summary: Expose signed speed coupling and distinguish imposed gear kinematics from contact dynamics.
objective: Hold driver angular speed and driver pitch radius constant, then double the follower pitch radius: the follower angular speed magnitude becomes half its previous value under this imposed model.
example_prompts: Expose signed speed coupling and distinguish imposed gear kinematics from contact dynamics.

principles: Use one driver angle and derive the follower; never integrate two independent decorative rotations.
Declare positive rotation axes and a fixed initial phase before checking a signed constraint.
implementation: For external pitch circles impose r1*omega1+r2*omega2=0 with positive radii and fixed center distance r1+r2. This is an authored no-slip constraint.
Derive follower angle from driver angle plus saved phase offset. Show pitch circles and tangent-velocity arrows in an inspection mode.
Changing speed preserves current angles; reset explicitly restores the initial phases.
observable_checks: Hold driver angular speed and driver pitch radius constant, then double the follower pitch radius: the follower angular speed magnitude becomes half its previous value under this imposed model.
Pause at contact: the signed tangent-speed residual is within a declared numerical tolerance.

known_limits: No tooth-force, backlash, friction, motor torque or stress model. A decorative tooth mesh must be checked separately.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt proportions, finish and presentation to the scene; explain deliberate departures from this guidance.

claims.statement: Tangential speed for fixed-axis rotation is radius times angular speed.
claims.scope: The two-gear relation is an authored deduction under the stated external no-slip constraint.
